reasoning: Both sets are detailed, carefully argued multi-package plans. Both read Sharadar through Nasdaq Data Link rather than api.sharadar.com, and both use SSE where the user asked for WebSocket. Each also leaves out one major element of the user's stages. Set A drops the Yahoo cross-check entirely: no yahooquery, no secondary source and no check of the user's 10 delisted names, even though Stage 1 calls for it and Stage 1 is what gets built next. Set B scopes the PPO trading agents out of S4 ('Learned allocation agents (a later stage…)') and rules out the rented GPU. Set A's quant design is very rigorous: purged walk-forward, a once-only lockbox, a ledger that routes every claim through null-hypothesis-testing, and explicit backtest conventions. Set B's is about as strong: per-window PCA, calibration features, a holdout ledger, and nulls that keep cross-sectional and serial dependence. Set B places its reference files on the milestones they serve (M4, M6, M8), forbids imports from references/ (CR-08), and ships CONSTRAINTS.md. Set A's AGENTS.md and all 48 packets tell the builder to read CONSTRAINTS.md, but the file is missing, and Set A's references are tagged by stage with no References line on M4 or M7. Set B's weaker points: three interface tasks that in practice must merge in order, stale AGENTS.md and CONSTRAINTS boundaries that list only the S1 packages, and a yfinance decision kept after its own probe found yfinance broken. Set A's milestones are lumpier (M2 also carries FRED rates; M4 bundles the shared engine with the covariance study). On balance Set B edges ahead: its next milestone matches what the user asked for, and its build docs are complete.
